title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, upgrade Node and deps, unify lint/test/release pipelines
author: Anya Patel
description: Summary: Consolidate multiple repository CI workflows into a smaller set of reusable jobs, upgrade Node to 20 across build/test pipelines, bump a set of developer dependencies (eslint, jest, turbo, actions/toolkit), and simplify release automation to reduce flakiness and maintenance. Motivation: We have diverging workflows across packages (sdk-python, sdk-js, redwood, infra) that increased CI maintenance overhead and caused inconsistent lint/test behavior. Upgrading to Node 20 and standardizing the workflow templates reduces cognitive load and fixes intermittent failures observed in nightly runs. Changes: - Introduce .github/workflows/ci-primary.yml which centralizes lint/test/build steps using a matrix for packages where applicable. - Replace multiple per-repo GitHub Actions with a single templated workflow and common composite actions in .github/actions/ci-helpers. - Upgrade Node from 18 -> 20 in all workflows and update lockfiles where required. - Bump top-level devDependencies: eslint@9.x, jest@29.x, turbo@1.6.x, @actions/core@2.x. - Swap some custom shell-based lint scripts to use the centralized node-based runner to get consistent rule resolution. - Replace a fragile release job that invoked external scripts with the enterprise release-bot action (internal) that supports dry-run and staged rollouts. - Add deterministic cache keys for node_modules and build artifacts to improve cache hit rates. - Add a migration note and small docs update to contributors/CI.md. Testing & verification: - Ran full CI against `main` with repository matrix (all packages) locally and in ephemeral branch. - Fixed a handful of package-level test flakiness by pinning test-time env vars and increasing Jest timeout in two slow tests. - Verified release automation in dry-run mode on a feature branch. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows into ci-primary.yml and helper composites - [x] Upgrade Node runtime to 20 in all job runners - [x] Bump devDependencies and regenerate lockfiles where required - [x] Add cache key improvements - [x] Add contributor docs update - [x] Address reviewer feedback and CI failures observed during iteration Rollout: Gradual merge to main with monitoring on CI runs; no runtime changes to production services. If CI regressions are observed, we can rollback the workflow file via a follow-up revert PR. Related: ENG-3241 (CI consolidation), ENG-3275 (release automation stability), linked PRs: #35842, #34567, #33101.

review_comments: Marco Liu (reviewer): Can we add a timeout/heartbeat to the matrix jobs? Some CI runners previously got stuck on a hung test. Action: added timeout-minutes and a keep-alive echo in the composite action.

Sana Rodriguez (reviewer): The eslint upgrade changes some autofix behavior; confirm CI applies fixes or fails. Author reply: CI now runs 'eslint --max-warnings=0' and the composite includes an autofix step for js/ts files before checking. Added note in contributors/CI.md.

Ethan Brooks (reviewer): Release step needs a dry-run-first gate to avoid accidental publishes. Author reply: release-bot composite runs dry-run + approval check; updated workflow to require manual approval in main for actual publish.

Marco Liu (reviewer): Observed one flaky integration test still failing in matrix element: tests/db-connection.spec.ts. Author reply: increased retry count and added deterministic test DB seeding; test green in subsequent run.
Sana Rodriguez (approver): LGTM after fixes. Approved and requested squash merge.

release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows into a single templated pipeline; upgraded GitHub Actions runners to Node 20; bumped devDependencies (eslint, jest, turbo); replaced bespoke release script with internal release-bot (dry-run support); improved cache keys and contributor CI docs. Impact: developer workflow should be more consistent; no runtime code changes. Rollback: revert this PR to restore previous workflows.
notes: Follow-ups: monitor CI for first 48 hours after merge; create small PR to revert action if cache regressions observed.
This PR reduces maintenance surface for infra team and should lower CI flakiness over time.
